all_18_original_unnumbered_groups.proposed_source_signature: Output a feasible decision before current feedback; comparator regret is the same played-loss sum minus fixed-comparator loss. Sublinear regret implies asymptotic average comparison.
Extended domain is {x:f(x)<+infinity}, allowing minus-infinity values; indicator is zero on V and plus-infinity otherwise; finite indicator-augmented losses enforce feasible actions.
Convex epigraph implies convex effective domain; indicator convex iff V convex; convex no-minus-infinity f plus indicator of convex V is convex.

Nonnegative weighted linear combinations preserve convexity. Precise extended-real arithmetic versus finite real-function scope needs explicit reconciliation; proof-as-exercise does not make this optional.
Affine precomposition preserves convexity; exact object/function codomain and assumptions require statement-level audit.
For real-valued convex f and convex nondecreasing g, g composed with f is convex; proof left as exercise remains required.
Pointwise supremum of convex functions is convex. Empty/unbounded families and real versus extended-real supremum conventions need exact reconciliation, not silent extra boundedness.
Under Theorem2.8 regularity, a feasible interior point minimizes over V iff its ambient gradient is zero.

Constant-step regret requires no finite domain diameter and retains the negative terminal distance. Variable-step proof needs distance control. Later unbounded-domain failure discussion points to Chapter5, without a separate explicit Chapter2 lower-bound statement.

For fixed positive distance and squared-gradient-energy coefficients, minimize A/(2 eta)+eta B/2 at sqrt(A/B), obtaining sqrt(A B). This is algebraic oracle minimization, not a causal choice of eta using future gradients; degenerate coefficients require boundary records.
Using diameter D and gradient norm bound L, minimize D^2/(2 eta)+eta L^2 T/2 at D/(L sqrt(T)) and derive D L sqrt(T). Requires positive denominator quantities and T>=1; same real run as Algorithm2.1.
Every real sublevel closed iff extended-real function is lower semicontinuous in the source Euclidean setting; source also states Hausdorff generalization.
For proper convex f, subdifferential outside effective domain is empty and dom(partial f) is contained in dom f. Properness supplies a finite witness excluding impossible +infinity support.

A proper convex function has a subgradient at every point of the ordinary interior of its effective domain. Footnote stronger relative-interior statement is separately flagged for source-scope review; no automatic coverage claim.

Replace differentiability by subdifferentiability and actual selected gradients by actual legal subgradients in the same projected updates. Inherit sharp fixed and positive nonincreasing variable-step bounds and tuning, retaining terminal terms. A single-step consumer alone is insufficient.
